title: Biome-Independent AI

premises.name: Existence record
premises.statement: Every known instance of AI, intelligence, and computation exists within a biology-dependent technosphere.
premises.revision_trigger: a single verified instance of AI persisting without biological dependency closure

premises.name: Qualification record
premises.statement: No biome-independent AI has been qualified over temporal periods with dependency closure, fault injection, environmental qualification, long-duration life test, independent replication, MTBF, or margins.
premises.revision_trigger: publication of a qualification campaign meeting all listed criteria

premises.name: Biology is constitutive, not modulatory
premises.statement: Biology is embedded in the mechanisms of every supporting domain, not an add-on.

domains.claim: microorganisms seed and template ore deposition
organisms central to formation and weathering

premises.revision_trigger: demonstration of a closed-loop abiotic substitute for any listed domain, integrated and tested

inference_rules.name: Burden shift
inference_rules.statement: If a claim asserts X can exist without Y, and every known X depends on Y, and no alternative has been qualified, then the burden of proof lies with the claimant.

inference_rules.name: Qualification requirement
inference_rules.statement: A system property is not established until it has scope, dependencies, test articles, durations, failure modes, margins, and replication.

inference_rules.name: No-proof-of-impossibility fallback
inference_rules.statement: Absence of proof of impossibility does not constitute support for possibility.

inference_rules.name: Constitutive dependency
inference_rules.statement: If biology is a mechanism inside a dependency (not a modulator), removing it breaks the dependency unless an abiotic substitute is qualified.

derived_conclusions.statement: Biome-independent AI is UNQUALIFIED, not established.
derived_conclusions.consequence_note: treating it as established leads to engineering and epistemic commitments without test data

derived_conclusions.statement: Assumptions about AI's independence from biology require scrutiny before use in critical systems.
Biology is a load-bearing component of the systems AI currently depends on; it cannot be assumed away.
derived_conclusions.consequence_note: if acted against: building critical systems on an unqualified independence assumption risks irreversible commitment

derived_conclusions.statement: This record does not prove biome-independent AI is impossible. It proves it is unqualified.

failure_record.note: These are failures of the assessor (the model), not the author of the argument.

entries.statement: Computation can run on non-biological hardware
AI can exist without the biome in principle

entries.violation: substitute for one dependency does not equal closure

entries.statement: No proof of impossibility used as soft support

revision_triggers: A biome-independent AI system completes a multi-year, fault-injected, independently replicated qualification campaign.
A closed-loop abiotic substitute is qualified for every domain in P3, integrated, and tested.
A verified instance of AI persists without biological dependency closure (revises P1).
A domain in P3 is shown to have an abiotic mechanism sufficient in isolation, integrated with the others (revises P3).

consequence_classes.RECOVERABLE: revising an assumption costs time or rework
consequence_classes.COSTLY: revising costs capability, funding, or credibility
consequence_classes.TERMINAL: revising costs the system, the mission, or irreversibility
